2026-11-28.title: Saturday after the Sunday of the Annunciation · St Catherine
readings: A father in Christ through the gospel
2026-11-28.alt: St Catherine of Alexandria, virgin and martyr. Her cult is ancient, but the details of her life come from Legend and cannot be verified.
2026-11-28.verse: It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown upon the ground, is the smallest of all the seeds on earth; yet when it is sown it grows up and becomes the greatest of all shrubs, and puts forth large branches, so that the birds of the air can make nests in its shade.
theo: Paul writes as a father, not a schoolmaster: “though you might have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. Indeed, in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.” He sends Timothy to remind them of his ways, and warns those who are puffed up: “the kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power.” Spiritual fatherhood and motherhood are a great gift in the Church: parents, godparents, priests and catechists who give birth to faith in others.

The kingdom, Jesus says, is like a mustard seed, the smallest of seeds, which becomes a great shrub where birds nest in its shade. Ezekiel had seen God plant a tender shoot that became a noble cedar. The Church began with twelve men and a few women; in India it began with one apostle on the coast of Kerala. On the last Saturday before the new liturgical season of fasting, we trust that small beginnings in God's hands bear great fruit.

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes as a father, not a schoolmaster: though you might have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. Indeed, in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel. I appeal to you, then, be imitators of me (1 Corinthians 4:15–16). The kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power.

In the Gospel Jesus compares the Kingdom to a mustard seed: when sown upon the ground it is the smallest of all seeds, yet it grows up and puts forth large branches, so that the birds of the air can make nests in its shade (Mark 4:30–32).

Today the Malankara Church remembers St Catherine. Our Church too began like a mustard seed, and after the reunion of 1930 it grew to give shade to many. Let us thank the spiritual fathers and mothers who handed on the faith to us, and let us become a father or mother in faith to someone. Amen.
